text:
matt_ae: Heads up 1 StrataHoldings wants a 4yr commitment but asked for net180 and annual invoices only. Theyre asking for 30% off list and want POC waived. Need deal desk + finance input.

sasha_salesops: tagging @diego_finance @zoe_dealdesk. Net180 is far outside standard. Any precedent? They want invoicing to local EU entity but payments from US treasury.

diego_finance: net180 is high risk. We'll need either a parent guarantee, an LC/bank guarantee, or 60% upfront to consider. Annual-only billing increases DSO exposure.

matt_ae: Customer says annual billing is non-negotiable for their procurement cadence. They can agree to 50% upfront instead of 60% if LC is provided for remainder. Also asking to remove POC line-item to speed procurement.

zoe_dealdesk: For a 30% concession we need heavy protections. Typical deals with extended terms get either 40-50% upfront + bank guarantee OR keep discount at 20%. Also need to lock in FX and tax routing.

kevin_se: POC waived, but we still need to provision a short validation run. Infra cost estimate ~ $32k. Recommend we add a non-refundable infra credit invoiced with upfront.

sasha_salesops: Proposal summary to vote on:
- Customer: StrataHoldings / StrataBank BU
- Term: 48 months
- List ARR: $2.2M/year
- Requested discount: 30%
- Billing: annual invoices (net180), payments from US treasury to payor in US, bill-to EU entity
- Upfront ask: 30% at signing (customer counter: 50% or LC)
- POC: waived, but infra credit $32k to be covered by upfront
- Conditions: bank guarantee or 50% upfront, legal approval for multi-entity billing

diego_finance: If they accept 50% upfront + LC for the rest, we can accept net120 on annual invoices. If they insist on net180 with only 30% upfront, CFO will decline. Need to run credit on parent and also request bank reference.

legalbot: Multi-entity billing ok if payer signs a guarantee. SOW must state invoicing entity, payer and recoverability. Also need export control check and AML language. If LC is used, attach instructions for beneficiary bank.

olga_cfo: I'm open to structured terms for strategic partners but not net180 unsecured. Approve conditionally with 50% upfront and either an LC for the balance or a parent guarantee. Also require holdback clause that allows us to revert discount if terms are breached.

matt_ae: I'll present two options to the customer: (A) 50% upfront + LC + 20% discount OR (B) 30% upfront + bank guarantee + 25% discount but moves to net120. Which is preferrable?

kevin_se: Prefer option A from infra standpoint. We get cash sooner and can schedule capacity.

zoe_dealdesk: Deal desk prefers A as well. We can sign off on 20% discount with 50% upfront; anything larger needs exec waiver.

sasha_salesops: I'll go back to procurement now. Key asks: confirm LC terms, confirm billing entity, confirm they accept infra credit invoiced with upfront. Will update thread when they respond.

matt_ae: Customer replied: procurement insists on annual payments only. They can do 50% upfront wired to our US account and will issue an irrevocable LC for the remaining 50% to a US beneficiary bank. They request the 30% discount if we accept LC vs cash.

diego_finance: With LC in place, and 50% upfront, finance can accept net120 on the annual invoices and reduce exposure. However discount cap with LC is 25% by policy; need CFO signoff for 30%.

olga_cfo: I can approve 30% discount only if the LC is irrevocable, confirmed by our bank, and we receive 50% cleared funds upfront. Also require escrow instruction for refund mechanics if SOW not met.

legalbot: Drafting amendment to contract: include LC beneficiary details, invoice schedule, refund/escrow clause, and guarantee language. Will share redline by EOD.

zoe_dealdesk: Provisional approval granted pending receipt of LC docs and upfront wire. Sales ops, pls attach credit run and bank confirmation.

sasha_salesops: Got it. Running bank confirmation and will drop docs here.

matt_ae: Thanks team. Moving to contracting. Will post final once LC and wire confirmed. :white_check_mark:
